CyberCloud.Analytics/clickhouseClusters.title: ClickHouse cluster
CyberCloud.Analytics/clickhouseClusters.summary: A managed ClickHouse cluster on the Altinity operator, with declared shards and replicas and a ClickHouse Keeper quorum. The schema is the tenant's.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the cluster is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new ClickHouse cluster to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The cluster's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the ClickHouse cluster.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new ClickHouse cluster to change it.

fields.name: keeperNodes
fields.label: Keeper nodes
fields.hint: Number of ClickHouse Keeper nodes. Keeper is a Raft quorum, so three is the smallest count that survives losing one and an even count tolerates no more failures than the odd count below it. One is offered for development and has no quorum at all.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: What the platform scrapes.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether ClickHouse's own Prometheus endpoint is served on port 9363. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". ⚠ It makes the metrics exist; the object that scrapes them is not built — see conformance.yaml § owed.

fields.name: replicas
fields.label: Replicas
fields.hint: Number of replicas per shard. This is the availability axis, and it only applies to tables the tenant creates as Replicated — the resource does not manage tables. Total server count is shards times replicas.

fields.name: shards
fields.label: Shards
fields.hint: Number of shards. This is the capacity and parallelism axis: a table's data is split across shards and a query fans out to all of them. ⚠ Resharding an existing table is not something the operator or this resource does, so growing this moves new data only.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory per ClickHouse server, either by preset or explicitly. The Keeper nodes are sized by the platform and are not affected.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory
fields.label: Memory
fields.hint: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 8Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Analytics uses the m1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 8 GiB.

fields.name: storage
fields.label: Storage
fields.hint: The data volume, per ClickHouse server.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class
fields.hint: StorageClass name for the ClickHouse servers and the Keeper nodes. Empty means the cluster default.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new ClickHouse cluster to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: Data volume size per ClickHouse server, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: ClickHouse version, which is also the ClickHouse Keeper version — the two share a release train and a wire protocol. Only long-term-support lines are offered; a new api-version is what adds a third.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Cache/redis.title: Valkey cache
CyberCloud.Cache/redis.summary: A managed Valkey cache with Sentinel failover, on spotahome/redis-operator. Valkey rather than Redis, per ADR-011; every Redis client works against it.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the cache is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Valkey cache to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The cache's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the RedisFailover.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Valkey cache to change it.

fields.name: maxmemoryPolicy
fields.label: Maxmemory policy
fields.hint: What happens when the cache reaches its memory limit. noeviction returns an error to the writer rather than dropping a key somebody is relying on.

fields.name: mode
fields.label: Mode
fields.hint: Replication topology. Sentinel is the only one this operator implements, and a client written against it is not portable to a sharded deployment, so it may not change after create.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Valkey cache to change it.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: What the platform scrapes.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the operator runs a metrics exporter beside every Valkey and every Sentinel pod.

fields.name: persistence
fields.label: Persistence
fields.hint: What survives a restart. None of the three settings makes a cache a database.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class
fields.hint: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Valkey cache to change it.

fields.name: fsync
fields.label: Fsync
fields.hint: How often the append-only file reaches the disk. Read only when the mode is AOF; everysec can lose the last second of writes.

fields.name: mode
fields.label: Mode
fields.hint: None keeps nothing, RDB snapshots periodically, AOF appends every write.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: Persistent volume size in Kubernetes quantity form. Unused when the mode is None, which keeps the data directory in memory.

fields.name: replicas
fields.label: Replicas
fields.hint: Number of Valkey instances, including the primary. One is a single point of failure and is offered for development only.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory, either by preset or explicitly.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory
fields.label: Memory
fields.hint: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset. It also sets maxmemory, so a cache evicts or refuses before the kernel kills the pod.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Caches use the m1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 8 GiB.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: Major Valkey version. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Communication/services/channe.title: Communication channel
CyberCloud.Communication/services/channe.summary: One channel a service sends on: which carrier, whose account pays, and what it may send and spend per day.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the channel is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Communication channel to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The channel's own settings.

fields.name: account
fields.label: Account
fields.hint: Whose carrier account pays. platform is marked up and needs no setup; tenant is the tenant's own contract, reached through accountRef and authRef.

fields.name: accountRef
fields.label: Account ref
fields.hint: For account: tenant — the vault handle of the account identifier (a Twilio account SID, a Meta business account id), as path#field.

fields.name: authRef
fields.label: Auth ref
fields.hint: For account: tenant — the vault handle of the authenticating value (an auth token, a bearer, an access secret), as path#field.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether sending on this channel is allowed at all. The kill switch: turning it off keeps the configuration and refuses every send.

fields.name: estimatedUnitCost
fields.label: Estimated unit cost
fields.hint: What one message is expected to cost, in currency, reserved before dispatch. Set it to the most expensive destination the channel sends to; an estimate that is too low turns the spend limit into a suggestion.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.hint: Which channel this configures. One service holds one configuration per kind.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Communication channel to change it.

fields.name: limits
fields.label: Limits
fields.hint: What the channel may send and spend per UTC day.

fields.name: currency
fields.label: Currency
fields.hint: ISO 4217, for the spend limit and the refusal that names it.

fields.name: maxMessagesPerDay
fields.label: Max messages per day
fields.hint: The most messages this channel dispatches in one UTC day. Zero — the default — means none: a channel with no limit is a channel that cannot send, on purpose.

fields.name: maxSpendPerDay
fields.label: Max spend per day
fields.hint: The most this channel spends in one UTC day, in currency. Zero means none.

fields.name: provider
fields.label: Provider
fields.hint: Which carrier implementation serves it — smtp is the one that ships, for kind: email — or empty for the one the platform registers for the kind. A name the platform has not registered refuses every send by that name.

fields.name: signingRef
fields.label: Signing ref
fields.hint: The vault handle of the carrier's webhook-signing value, when it signs its callbacks. A receipt that cannot be verified is data from the internet.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

fields.name: channel

fields.name: destination

CyberCloud.Communication/services/templa.title: Message template
CyberCloud.Communication/services/templa.summary: A named, versioned message body with typed variables. Every change appends a version; a send names the template and the version it wants.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the template is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Message template to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The template's own settings.

fields.name: body
fields.label: Body
fields.hint: The message text. A {name} is replaced by the argument of that name, left to right, and a substituted value is never re-scanned.
fields.placeholder: Your verification code is {code}. It expires in {minutes} minutes.

fields.name: channel
fields.label: Channel
fields.hint: Which channel the body is written for. A WhatsApp body is not an email body, and the channel decides whether carrier pre-approval is consulted at all.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Message template to change it.

fields.name: locale

fields.name: optionalVariables

fields.name: subject
fields.label: Subject

fields.name: variables
fields.label: Variables
fields.hint: The placeholders a send must supply. A send missing one is refused before any carrier is called.

fields.name: tags

CyberCloud.Compute/disks.title: Managed disk
CyberCloud.Compute/disks.summary: A blank data disk of a size and a storage class, provisioned on its own and attached to a virtual machine by name. It outlives the machine.

fields.name: location

fields.name: properties

CyberCloud.Compute/images.title: Image
CyberCloud.Compute/images.summary: A bootable disk image imported once into your resource group — one of the platform's Ubuntu and Debian cloud images, pinned by digest, or a container disk or HTTP address you supply — and cloned by every machine that boots from it.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the image is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Image to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The image's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster the image is imported into. A virtual machine can boot from it only in the same cluster and the same resource group, because a clone is a claim in one namespace copied from a claim beside it.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Image to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: The claim the image is imported into, in Kubernetes quantity form. It must hold the image's virtual size — 10Gi fits every catalogue image — and it is the smallest disk a machine booted from this image can have.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Image to change it.

fields.name: source
fields.label: Source
fields.hint: Where the bytes come from.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.hint: catalogue for one of the platform's own Linux cloud images, pinned by digest; url for an address you supply.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Image to change it.

fields.name: name

fields.hint: Which catalogue image, when kind is catalogue. ⚠ Linux only: Windows Server is a licensing arrangement and not in this catalogue — docs/plan/13 § Images and licensing.

fields.name: storageClass
fields.label: Storage class
fields.hint: The storage class the imported claim is on. Empty means the cluster's default, which on a bundle-installed cluster is the node-local class.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Image to change it.

CyberCloud.Compute/virtualMachines.title: Virtual machine
CyberCloud.Compute/virtualMachines.summary: A virtual machine on KubeVirt: a size from the platform catalogue, a root disk cloned from an image, managed disks by name, a tenant subnet, and cloud-init from a vault handle. Start, stop and restart are actions; stop releases compute and keeps every disk.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the machine is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Virtual machine to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The machine's own settings.

fields.name: cloudInit
fields.label: Cloud init
fields.hint: First-boot configuration, as cloud-init reads it.

fields.name: userData
fields.label: User data
fields.hint: A vault handle — path#field, optionally @version — whose value is the cloud-init user data: the #cloud-config with your users, SSH keys and packages. Resolved when the machine is rendered and written into a Secret the machine mounts; the value never enters this body. ⚠ The path must be under your own tenant's vault prefix, tenants/<tenantId>/; any other path is refused. Empty means no cloud-init at all.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster the machine runs in. Must be the one its image and its disks are in — nothing checks that, and a machine placed elsewhere clones a claim that is not there.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Virtual machine to change it.

fields.name: dataDisks
fields.label: Data disks
fields.hint: CyberCloud.Compute/disks resources attached to the machine, by name, in this resource group. A change attaches or detaches at the machine's next start. ⚠ A disk named os or cloudinit collides with the machine's own volumes and is refused.

fields.name: image
fields.label: Image
fields.hint: The CyberCloud.Compute/images resource the root disk is cloned from, by name, in this resource group. ⚠ The image must have finished importing: the machine waits for it and says so.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Virtual machine to change it.

fields.name: network
fields.label: Network
fields.hint: The tenant network the machine's interface joins. Both empty means the cluster's pod network.

fields.name: subnet
fields.label: Subnet
fields.hint: The subnet of that network the interface takes its address from, by name, or empty. ⚠ A name that is not a subnet of the network is refused by the fabric rather than by this API, and the machine never starts.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Virtual machine to change it.

fields.name: virtualNetwork
fields.label: Virtual network
fields.hint: The CyberCloud.Network/virtualNetworks resource in this resource group, by name, or empty.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Virtual machine to change it.

fields.name: osDiskSize
fields.label: Os disk size
fields.hint: The root disk, in Kubernetes quantity form. At least the image's own size; a clone into a smaller claim is refused by CDI, not by this API. ⚠ Immutable, for the reason a managed disk's size is.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Virtual machine to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: The machine's size, from the platform's sizing catalogue: s1.small is 1 vCPU and 4 GiB, and each rung doubles both. Changing it takes effect the next time the machine starts — KubeVirt reports RestartRequired until then.

CyberCloud.ContainerService/connectedClu.title: Connected Kubernetes cluster
CyberCloud.ContainerService/connectedClu.summary: A cluster you run yourself — on-prem, behind NAT, anywhere with outbound HTTPS — reached through an agent you install in it. Create it, run the install command it gives you, and place resources in it once it reports Succeeded.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the cluster is billed in. ⚠ Where the cluster physically is is the tenant's business; this is the region whose gateway the agent dials and whose silos hold the connection.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Connected Kubernetes cluster to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The connected cluster's own settings.

fields.name: distribution
fields.label: Distribution
fields.hint: What the cluster runs — k3s, kubeadm, OpenShift, a hosted service. Informational: the agent works against any conformant API server and nothing here changes what it does.

fields.name: heartbeatSeconds
fields.label: Heartbeat seconds
fields.hint: How often the agent reports in. Read when listInstallCommand is called: the command passes it to the chart and the platform repeats it in the welcome the agent adopts on every connection. A change after that takes effect on the next listInstallCommand — no re-install; the running agent adopts it on its next connection. ⚠ The platform calls a cluster Degraded after ninety seconds without a heartbeat (docs/plan/09 § Cluster connections), so a value above thirty leaves fewer than three chances for a packet to arrive.

fields.name: tags

CyberCloud.Monitor/workspaces.title: Monitor workspace
CyberCloud.Monitor/workspaces.summary: A tenancy in the platform's metrics, logs and traces stores, with its own retention, quota, ingest key and read-only datasource endpoints.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the workspace is billed in, and the region whose telemetry stores hold its data.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Monitor workspace to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The workspace's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The regional cluster whose telemetry data plane serves this workspace. ⚠ Nothing is deployed into it: a workspace is a tenancy in stores the platform already runs, and this is where its ingest routing is published.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Monitor workspace to change it.

fields.name: purgeProtection
fields.label: Purge protection
fields.hint: Whether this workspace may be destroyed before its seven-day recovery window is out. Once true it stays true for the rest of the workspace's life, and a purge is refused while it is set.

fields.name: quota
fields.label: Quota
fields.hint: What the workspace may take in per day, and what happens when it takes in more.

fields.name: cardinalityCap
fields.label: Cardinality cap
fields.hint: Distinct values one metric label may take before the series carrying it are rejected. The rejection names the offending label — docs/plan/16 § Ingest — because a rejection nobody can diagnose is one the client just retries.

fields.name: logsGbPerDay
fields.label: Logs gb per day
fields.hint: Log lines accepted per day, in gibibytes.

fields.name: metricsGbPerDay
fields.label: Metrics gb per day
fields.hint: Metric samples accepted per day, in gibibytes. This is the first factor of what the workspace draws against the subscription's storage quota; the second is the retention tier.

fields.name: overQuotaSampleRate
fields.label: Over quota sample rate
fields.hint: The percentage of data still accepted once a signal is over its daily allowance. ⚠ It cannot be zero: docs/plan/16 requires that going over quota samples at a visible rate rather than dropping silently, and zero is a silent drop spelled as a rate.

fields.name: seriesCap
fields.label: Series cap
fields.hint: Active metric series the workspace may hold at once. One tenant putting a request id in a metric label is how a shared time-series database dies, so this is a ceiling rather than a guideline.

fields.name: tracesGbPerDay
fields.label: Traces gb per day
fields.hint: Spans accepted per day, in gibibytes.

fields.name: retention
fields.label: Retention
fields.hint: How long each signal is kept. Priced per tier — docs/plan/16 § Cost and retention honesty.

fields.name: logs
fields.label: Logs
fields.hint: Logs retention tier: short is 7 days, standard 30, extended 90. ⚠ Shortening this under an existing workspace destroys the lines already outside the new window, and the reconciler refuses the change rather than applying it.

fields.name: metrics
fields.label: Metrics
fields.hint: Metrics retention tier: short is 15 days, standard 90, extended 400. ⚠ Shortening this under an existing workspace destroys the samples already outside the new window, and the reconciler refuses the change rather than applying it.

fields.name: traces
fields.label: Traces

CyberCloud.Monitor/workspaces/alertRules.title: Alert rule
CyberCloud.Monitor/workspaces/alertRules.summary: A condition over the workspace's metrics or logs, evaluated on a schedule; when it holds for long enough the action group is told through a Communication service, and again when it stops.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the rule is evaluated in — the workspace's.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Alert rule to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The rule's own settings.

fields.name: actionGroup
fields.label: Action group
fields.hint: Who is told, and how.

fields.name: channel
fields.label: Channel
fields.hint: Which of that service's channels carries it. The service must have the channel configured and enabled, or every notification is refused by name.

fields.name: notifyOnResolve
fields.label: Notify on resolve
fields.hint: Whether the recipients are told when the condition stops holding, as well as when it starts.

fields.name: recipients
fields.label: Recipients
fields.hint: Where it goes — addresses or E.164 numbers, one send each, every one checked against the service's suppression list before dispatch. At least one and at most 20; a list outside that is refused when the rule is reconciled.

fields.name: service
fields.label: Service
fields.hint: The CyberCloud.Communication/services resource the notification is sent through, as its full resource id path. It must be in this tenant.

fields.name: condition
fields.label: Condition
fields.hint: What is asked, and what answer counts.

fields.name: lookbackSeconds
fields.label: Lookback seconds
fields.hint: How far back the query may read, in seconds. Capped at a day: the look-back is the query's cost, and the cap is the platform's, not the tenant's.

fields.name: operator
fields.label: Operator
fields.hint: How a value is compared with the threshold.

fields.name: query
fields.label: Query
fields.hint: The query, verbatim. It must produce numbers; the rule fires when any of them satisfies the operator against the threshold.

fields.name: signal
fields.label: Signal

fields.name: threshold
fields.label: Threshold

fields.name: evaluation
fields.label: Evaluation

fields.name: forSeconds
fields.label: For seconds
fields.hint: How long the condition must hold before the rule fires, in seconds. Zero fires on the first evaluation that meets it; 300 ignores anything shorter than five minutes.

fields.name: intervalSeconds
fields.label: Interval seconds
fields.hint: How often the condition is evaluated, in seconds. A multiple of 60: the evaluator ticks once a minute and a rule at 300 is evaluated on every fifth tick. Anything else is refused when the rule is reconciled.

fields.name: severity
fields.label: Severity
fields.hint: How loud: critical pages somebody, error is looked at today, warning this week, informational is worth knowing.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags

CyberCloud.Network/virtualNetworks/loadB.title: Load balancer
CyberCloud.Network/virtualNetworks/loadB.summary: An L4 TCP proxy on an address inside a virtual network, spreading connections across a pool of workload addresses with health checks and a connection limit.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the load balancer is billed in. ⚠ It must be the region its virtual network is in — nothing checks that, because the network's own region is not readable from here.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Load balancer to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The load balancer's own settings.

fields.name: backend
fields.label: Backend
fields.hint: Where the connections go.

fields.name: addresses
fields.label: Addresses
fields.hint: The workload addresses to balance across, comma separated — for example 10.20.1.11,10.20.1.12. ⚠ Addresses and not resource ids: there is no service discovery and no DNS inside a virtual network, so an address is what a tenant has for their own workloads. At most 32.

fields.name: port
fields.label: Port
fields.hint: The TCP port every backend address is reached on. ⚠ One port for the whole pool: a pool whose members listen on different ports is two pools.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster the proxy runs in. ⚠ It must be the cluster the virtual network was created in: a proxy in another cluster has no route into this network at all.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Load balancer to change it.

fields.name: frontend
fields.label: Frontend
fields.hint: The address and port workloads connect to.

fields.name: port
fields.label: Port
fields.hint: The TCP port the proxy listens on. ⚠ There is no protocol setting: HAProxy does not proxy UDP in any version, so every rule here is TCP.

fields.name: v4
fields.label: V4
fields.hint: The IPv4 address the proxy answers on, inside the subnet's range. ⚠ Required, and it is the one thing about this resource a tenant must choose: there is no DNS inside a virtual network, so an address nobody picked is an address nothing can be pointed at. A bare address and never a prefix.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Load balancer to change it.

fields.name: v6
fields.label: V6
fields.hint: The IPv6 address the proxy also answers on, or empty. ⚠ Lower case only, for the fabric's reason. It must be inside the subnet's IPv6 range, which means the subnet has to have one.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Load balancer to change it.

fields.name: health
fields.label: Health
fields.hint: How a backend is decided to be up. ⚠ Checking cannot be turned off — a proxy that sends connections to a dead server is worse than no proxy.

fields.name: healthyAfter
fields.label: Healthy after
fields.hint: How many successful probes put a backend back into the pool.

fields.name: intervalSeconds
fields.label: Interval seconds
fields.hint: How often each backend is probed with a TCP connection.

fields.name: unhealthyAfter
fields.label: Unhealthy after
fields.hint: How many failed probes take a backend out of the pool.

fields.name: limits
fields.label: Limits
fields.hint: What the proxy refuses rather than passes on.

fields.name: maxConnections
fields.label: Max connections
fields.hint: How many connections the frontend accepts at once. ⚠ Further connections wait in the kernel's accept queue rather than being refused, so this is a back-pressure setting rather than a firewall. It is also applied per backend server.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory for the proxy.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: How much the proxy pod gets. An L4 proxy is mostly kernel work, so the small row carries far more than its size suggests; the larger rows are for many long-lived connections.

fields.name: subnet
fields.label: Subnet
fields.hint: The subnet of this virtual network the proxy sits on. ⚠ The proxy gets an address from it, so the frontend address below must be inside its range. A name that is not a subnet of this network is refused by the fabric rather than by the API, and the proxy pod never schedules.

fields.name: home
fields.label: Home
fields.hint: The persistent home directory. The only part of a console that survives an idle reclaim.

fields.name: retentionDays
fields.label: Retention days
fields.hint: How long $HOME is kept after the console was last attached to. ⚠ Nothing sweeps on it yet — it is carried so that a console created today is swept correctly by whatever does.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: The size of $HOME. It grows and never shrinks: a PersistentVolumeClaim refuses a decrease at the API.

fields.name: identity
fields.label: Identity
fields.hint: Who the shell runs as.

fields.name: principalId
fields.label: Principal id
fields.hint: The managed identity every command in this shell acts as. It may not be changed: a console whose identity moved would have an audit trail describing a shell that no longer exists.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Cloud terminal to change it.

fields.name: image
fields.label: Image
fields.hint: Which shell image to run.

fields.name: variant
fields.label: Variant
fields.hint: default carries every tool in docs/plan/19's table and takes about 40 seconds to pull cold; minimal carries shells, editors, cyc and kubectl and starts in about 8. The repository and the digest are the platform's.

fields.name: network
fields.label: Network
fields.hint: What the shell may reach. Nothing may ever reach the shell.

fields.name: egress
fields.label: Egress
fields.hint: Internet lets the shell reach public addresses as well as this subscription's own workloads and DNS — a shell that cannot git clone is not a shell. TenantOnly removes the public half and leaves the rest.

fields.name: session
fields.label: Session
fields.hint: When a shell stops. Both numbers are ceilings a tenant may lower and neither may be turned off.

fields.name: idleTimeoutMinutes
fields.label: Idle timeout minutes
fields.hint: How long a shell may sit with nobody typing into it before it is reclaimed. The home volume survives; the pod does not. ⚠ There is no value meaning never — an idle terminal is a tenant paying for something they closed.

fields.name: maxDurationHours
fields.label: Max duration hours
fields.hint: The longest a single shell may run, busy or not. Enforced by the kubelet through the pod's own deadline, so it holds even when nothing of this platform is running.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory for the shell.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: How much a shell gets. The ladder stops at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB, which is docs/plan/19's ceiling for this row — a workload that needs more needs a cluster and a job rather than a terminal.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

managementGroup.title: Management group
managementGroup.summary: The optional tree above the subscription, for role inheritance. docs/plan/06 § The hierarchy.

fields.name: displayName
fields.label: Display name
fields.help: The name a person reads. Optional; defaults to the group's name.

fields.name: managementGroup
fields.label: Management group
fields.help: The parent group, by name. Optional: absent or empty hangs the group off the tenant. ⚠ Set at creation and not movable — a later PUT naming a different parent is a 409. The tree is capped at six levels.

subscription.title: Subscription
subscription.summary: The billing and quota boundary. docs/plan/06 § The hierarchy.

fields.name: displayName
fields.label: Display name
fields.help: The name on an invoice and in every scope picker. Required — a subscription identified only by its GUID is one nobody can pick out of a list.

fields.name: managementGroup
fields.label: Management group
fields.help: The management group to assign the subscription to, by name. Optional. ⚠ Absent leaves the assignment unchanged on a subscription that exists and means the tenant root on one that does not; the empty string moves the subscription to the tenant root. Assigning needs write on the group as well as on the tenant. docs/plan/06 § The hierarchy.

resourceGroup.title: Resource group
resourceGroup.summary: The lifecycle boundary — what a resource is created in. docs/plan/06 § The hierarchy.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.help: The region the group's resources default to. Required, and there is no platform-wide default to fall back on: a group whose region were guessed would place a tenant's data somewhere nobody chose.
